title: Problem Overview
content: Erdős Problem #686: Can every integer N ≥ 2 be written as ∏(m+i)/∏(n+i) for some k ≥ 2 and m ≥ n+k? From [Er79d]. Products of consecutive integers relate to factorials and binomials. This problem cannot be resolved with a finite computation. OPEN.
mathContext: The ratio equals C(m+k,k)/C(n+k,k). Finding the right (n,m,k) triple for each N requires subtle divisibility arguments.

title: Consecutive Products
content: consecutiveProduct(n,k) = ∏_{i=1}^k (n+i) defines the product of k consecutive integers starting from n+1. Two axioms establish the connections: it equals (n+k)!/n! (factorial form) and k! * C(n+k,k) (binomial form). Three examples verified by native_decide.
mathContext: The fundamental building block. Products of consecutive integers have rich divisibility properties arising from their factorial/binomial structure.

title: Ratio Expression
content: ratioExpression(n,m,k): P(m,k)/P(n,k) computed as a rational number. IsIntegerRatio captures the divisibility condition P(n,k) | P(m,k) needed for the ratio to be a natural number.
mathContext: Working over ℚ for exact division. The ratio equals C(m+k,k)/C(n+k,k) since the k! factors cancel.

title: Main Conjecture (OPEN)
content: IsRepresentable(N,n,m,k): k ≥ 2, m ≥ n+k, ratio = N. Representable(N): ∃ such triple. ErdosConjecture686: ∀ N ≥ 2, Representable(N). The constraint k ≥ 2 excludes trivial single-factor ratios, and m ≥ n+k ensures non-overlapping ranges.
mathContext: The problem asks about universality of this representation. Not every pair of constraints (n,k) works for every N, so existence across all N is non-trivial.

title: Structural Properties
content: numerator_gt_denominator: when m ≥ n+k, each factor (m+i) > (n+i), so P(m,k) > P(n,k). ratio_gt_one: the ratio exceeds 1 under the problem constraints. These ensure the representation yields integers ≥ 2.
mathContext: These structural properties justify the problem constraints: they guarantee the ratio is a positive integer greater than 1.

title: Example: N = 6
content: Verified: ratioExpression 0 2 2 = 6, meaning (3)(4)/(1)(2) = 12/2 = 6. This confirms at least one integer has the desired representation.
mathContext: Computational verification via native_decide. This is the simplest non-trivial case.

title: Follow-Up: Fixed Parameter Sets
content: RepresentableSet(n,k) = {N | ∃ m ≥ n+k, ratio = N}: the set of integers representable with fixed initial parameters. ratio_mono: the ratio increases with m. representable_set_infinite: this set is infinite for k ≥ 2.
mathContext: Erdős's secondary question: for fixed n and k, what can be said about the representable set? The monotonicity shows it grows without bound.

title: Connection to Problem #677
content: Problem #677 asks about writing integers as products of consecutive integers (without ratios). We define problem_677_special_case and prove product_implies_ratio: any integer expressible as a product of consecutive integers is automatically representable as a ratio (with denominator range starting at 0). This shows #686 generalizes #677.
mathContext: The product-to-ratio reduction shows that the ratio representation is strictly more general than the product representation.

title: Summary: OPEN
content: erdos_686_statement (proved by simp): ErdosConjecture686 ↔ ∀ N ≥ 2, ∃ n m k, k ≥ 2 ∧ m ≥ n+k ∧ ratio = N. The theorem unfolds the definition chain to show the conjecture's equivalent explicit form. Problem remains OPEN since [Er79d].
mathContext: The simp proof unfolds ErdosConjecture686, Representable, and IsRepresentable to show logical equivalence with the explicit statement.
